Well, one suggestion I'd give immediately is to use an ArrayList object or something to contain your newly created serverThreads that way, later on, you can manage things on a client-to-client basis a lot easier. You'll need to add IDs to each client for this to work the way you'll intend later. On your client, the way that I would design it is to have your client have a thread to continually scan for messages from the server. That way, your messages can update on the clientside as they are received.

Pretty much, your server should just act as a middle man between clients. The reason I think separating the server from client functionality is important is because looking at it as a client-client interaction is easier. The server is a middleman for interactions between clients, and clients are targeted by other clients using IDs or some other system. You can even have your "server client" by just having a client instance running through your server program.

What you'll want to do to get your readers/writers working, now, is to have clients connect to your server, obtain a thread ID and client thread/server thread on the server, and have that put in a data structure on the server. When a client wants to send a message to another client, the client sends that to the server socket, server receives it, looks for the ID it is intended to go to, and sends it from the server to that client by looking up the receiver in the data structure. From there, you handle messages on the client end.

I hope that helps clear it up a little bit. That way of readers/writers will make it easier to scale and easier to have many rooms or many users, and probably make it easier for you to implement. But yeah, for the server text displaying for the client, having a thread running on the client that scans for messages from the server separate from the code that sends messages to the server should work. Anything more specific is the fun learning part. ;)
